Thanks for the loop. Quick product take: we can support a temporary guardrail that combines an automatic fallback to the previous known-good variant and a pinned-version hold for the customer for 72 hours. A few constraints to call out so legal/ops understand:

- Automatic fallback: recommended pattern is an automated health-check gate (p99 and error-rate) with an immediate rollback action plus a 5-minute cooldown to avoid flapping.
- Pinning: we expose a 'pin_until' timestamp on the route that prevents automated upgrades; manual overrides remain for platform admins.
- SLA impact: rollbacks themselves don't erase telemetry; for billing/SLA we can mark the incident as 'mitigated by rollback' and exclude the rollback window from SLA breach calculations if both parties agree in writing before launch.

I'll attach a short draft of the runbook and the config snippet. Marissa — can you validate the cooldown and KV cache invalidation behavior during a rollback?

-laura
Director, Product

attachments: canary_runbook_v1.md

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot launch concern — Pilot runbook & rollback mechanics

Quick engineering note — validated the approach. Practical details to include in the runbook:

- Trigger logic: p99 delta > 200ms sustained over 10 minutes OR error-rate increase > 1.5x baseline triggers automatic fallback.
- Fallback behavior: route switches to previous variant within ~8-12s; KV cache TTL remains valid but we perform conservative cache invalidation for 60s to avoid mixing model states.
- Pin semantics: 'pin_until' prevents any automated Canary promotion; manual unpin requires two platform-admin approvals (audit trail).
- Audit & telemetry: we will emit a rollback_event with rollback_reason, pre/post p99, and model_variant IDs. This can be surfaced to Atlas's dashboard.

I've put the runbook (canary_runbook_v1.md) in the linked Drive folder and attached a minimal MOP snippet. If legal needs specific wording on SLA carveouts, Naomi please advise.

—Marissa
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot launch concern — canary rollback during peak windows

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks for raising this. Summary of what Redwood can commit for the AtlasHealth pilot starting Monday:

1) Temporary guardrail: we will enable an automatic fallback that re-routes to the previously stable model when either 
   - p99 latency increases by >200ms for a rolling 10-minute window, or
   - error rate increases by >1.5x baseline.
2) Pin window: AtlasHealth route will be set with pin_until = UTC(launch_time + 72h). This prevents automatic promotions; manual rollbacks/unpins require two-platform-admin approval.
3) Cooldown & cache: rollback includes a 5-minute cooldown with conservative cache invalidation (60s) to avoid inconsistent KV state.
4) SLA carveout: Redwood will treat rollback periods as mitigated incidents and exclude the rollback window from SLA breach calculations provided Atlas signs the attached MUA amendment before launch.
5) Runbook: link to the runbook and MOP is here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz-canary-runbook (runbook attached to this thread).

Next steps: if this matches Atlas' needs, could you confirm by EOD Sunday so Naomi can circulate the MUA language and procurement can sign?

Best,
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
